title: Let's Encrypt cuts certificate lifetimes to 64 days starting February 2027
gist: Let's Encrypt will cut free TLS certificate lifetimes from 90 to 64 days on Feb 10, 2027, with 45-day defaults in 2028 and authorization reuse shrinking to 10 days then seven hours. Operators on hardcoded renewal schedules risk outages unless they adopt ACME ARI automation.

insights.claim: Let's Encrypt will cut certificate lifetimes from 90 to 64 days starting February 10, 2027, with opt-in testing from October 14.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Forces operational changes across a large share of the web's TLS deployments.
insights.locator: Let’s Encrypt is continuing a push

insights.claim: Let's Encrypt plans 45-day default certificates in 2028 and says lifespans will keep shrinking.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Manual certificate management becomes untenable; automation tooling demand rises.
insights.quote: the lifespans will only continue to get shorter as time goes on, with 45-day defaults planned to follow in 2028

insights.claim: Authorization reuse periods will shrink from 30 days to 10 days and eventually to seven hours by 2028.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Validation must become near-real-time, stressing cached-validation workflows.

insights.claim: Shorter lifetimes aim to push users to full ACME automation with ARI, just as 90-day certs originally forced renewal automation and HTTPS adoption.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Policy is used as a lever to force automation, benefiting certificate lifecycle tooling.

insights.claim: Shorter validity limits damage from private key theft or mis-issued certificates.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Security rationale makes the trend durable across CAs.

insights.claim: Deployments on fixed renewal offsets (e.g., renewing at 83, 80 or 60 days) or manual processes risk unexpected expirations and downtime after the deadline.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Outage risk for laggard enterprises in early 2027.

insights.claim: Let's Encrypt recommends renewing at two-thirds of lifespan, verifying ARI support, and setting expiration/renewal-failure notifications.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.locator: Let’s Encrypt is getting this information
